verdict.rationale: Abacum documents scenario planning where base, bull and bear versions share a base and an assumption change moves cash along with revenue and hiring. It also builds cash flow statements from live actuals, so cash impact per scenario is plausible. But the evidence never mentions burn rate, runway, or a zero-cash date being computed per scenario. Missing for 10: explicit burn and runway metrics per scenario, a projected zero-cash date and how it shifts between scenarios, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, burn and cash runway are computed per scenario, so I can see how a decision moves the zero-cash date

citations.quote: Build base, bull and bear off the same base version. Change an assumption and watch revenue, hiring and cash move together.
Abacum builds P&L, balance sheet and cash flow off live actuals from your ERP
Connect actuals, assumptions, forecasts, and scenarios in one governed workspace
